sentences.text: The name Latenivenatrix means "hiding huntress" and it is a genus of large troodontid dinosaur.
This species is distinguished by a retroverted pubis forming a 17° angle and an anteriorly curved pubic shaft.
The frontal bones of Latenivenatrix are triangular in shape and feature a single deep groove on the frontonasal contact surface.
Latenivenatrix possesses a concave anterior surface on metatarsal III.
A hatchling specimen of Latenivenatrix shows evidence of a congenital defect causing a twisted jaw.
A parietal bone from Latenivenatrix bears a pathological aperture that may indicate injury or disease.
The genus Latenivenatrix was described by van der Reest and Currie in 2017.
The type specimen of Latenivenatrix was originally described in 1969 by Dale Alan Russell.
The holotype of Latenivenatrix was collected in 1968 by Irene Vanderloh from the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada.
As a derived troodontid, Latenivenatrix was likely a semi-omnivorous biped that had lost the ability to fly.
Researchers have debated the cause of a pathological aperture in a Latenivenatrix parietal bone, with hypotheses ranging from a cyst to a bite wound.
Latenivenatrix is classified as a derived troodontid within the subfamily Troodontinae, likely related to Asian contemporaries like Linhevenator and Philovenator.
The time range for Latenivenatrix is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether Latenivenatrix is a distinct genus or a junior synonym of Stenonychosaurus.
Some analyses have considered Latenivenatrix mcmasterae to be a junior synonym of Stenonychosaurus inequalis due to overlapping stratigraphic positions and lack of definitive diagnostic characters.
